body: I should probably add that the current version of the server is using the "old" Netty HTTP/2 API to build our pipeline.
@Scottmitch can you please have a look ?
@nhnFreespirit - Are you doing renegotiations, and is this pause related to handshake/setup time? Or does this pause occur after the handshake is setup and you are sending application data?

@Scottmitch I looked at this problem briefly today with Wireshark and it looks like the pause is after the handshake is complete and application data has started being sent. I am currently working on decrypting the data being sent back and forth between our client and server so that I can see where exactly things are getting blocked. I should have more information regarding that tomorrow.
@fsareshwala - Thanks for the update. Keep me posted. It would be nice to keep some of this optimization and fix the missing pieces but if necessary we can also revert it.

I have a bit more information to share. We were able to decrypt the data being transferred between our services.

In the Wireshark trace below, we have two services communicating with each other. The netty server is listening on port `8443` and the ssl client is using port `55507`. Packet 75 is where the client sends its request. It receives no response from the netty server for about 9 seconds at which point the client sends a `PING` request. Receiving no response from the netty server for another 0.5 seconds, the client closes the stream.


I'll try and put together some minimal code that will reproduce this.
thanks for the update @fsareshwala. I'm assuming there a missing headers frame before packet 75?

@Scottmitch I am working on getting a reproducer up for you but I have some things I need to take care of first internally at Twitter. This is still an important task for me so I will get back to it as soon as I can. Just wanted to you let you know :).
